correctness.summary: Run never computes any bipartite matching; 'matching' stays 0 and the method always returns n. The minimum path cover of any DAG with >=1 edge is strictly less than n, so the result is wrong for every non-trivial input. The head/next/to/dist/queue parameters are ignored.
correctness.triggeringInput: DAG 0->1 (n=2): minimum path cover is 1, but with matching==0 the method returns n - 0 = 2.
correctness.rootCause: The Hopcroft-Karp / augmenting-path body is unimplemented. After 'int matching = 0;' and resetting match[i]=-1, no edges are ever processed, so matching remains 0 and the return is n - 0 = n.
correctness.suggestedFix: Implement bipartite matching (Hopcroft-Karp BFS/DFS using head/next/to/match/dist/queue) to compute the actual matching count, then return n - matching.

perf.summary: Run is a non-functional stub: it never computes the bipartite matching, so it always returns n.
perf.currentCost: matching is initialized to 0 and never updated; the documented Hopcroft-Karp augmentation is absent. head/next/to/dist/queue parameters are unused. Result is always n - 0 = n, which is wrong for any DAG with edges.
perf.proposedChange: Implement Hopcroft-Karp (or Kuhn) augmenting-path matching using the provided head/next/to adjacency, match (size 2n for split L/R or two arrays), dist and queue (BFS layering) buffers, then return n - matching. Use AggressiveInlining only on leaf helpers, not the whole driver.
perf.rationale: Correctness first; once implemented, Hopcroft-Karp gives O(E*sqrt(V)) which is the right asymptotic for min path cover via Dilworth, vastly better than naive O(V*E) Kuhn on dense inputs and the intended use of the dist/queue buffers.
perf.risk: This is a functional gap, not a micro-opt: current output is incorrect. Implementing it changes (fixes) behavior by design. Must respect house constraints (pointers, no exceptions).
